maria: Quick weirdness from a customer canary — quota attribution flips to the route hint when we also receive a legacy cost-center header. Logs show `quota_bucket=team-x route=eu-west fallback=true cost_center=acct-123` but the console shows credits taken from acct-123 instead of team-x. Anyone seen this?

sam: Yep saw a similar trace yesterday. Root cause looks like the order we normalize headers in the gateway: we apply route_hint first then merge quota headers, which lets the route override attribution.

kai: Oof — that ordering difference will bite TS/Go clients when we land the new routing header. If SDKs start emitting route_hint, older servers might mis-attribute.

jonas: Short-term patch: SDKs should sanitize/normalize header precedence client-side to match server semantics. Long-term: agree server should be deterministic and documented.

maria: To be concrete, propose SDKs add a small compatibility shim: if both `X-Route-Hint` and `X-Cost-Center` are present, send `X-Rwd-Attr-Prefer: cost_center` (opt-in) or drop `X-Route-Hint` when running against pre-compat control plane. Example Python shim: ```python
headers = {
  "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
  "X-Cost-Center": "acct-123",
}
# opt-in flag from env/SDK config
if sdk_config.get("compat_route_shim"):
  headers["X-Rwd-Attr-Prefer"] = "cost_center"
else:
  headers["X-Route-Hint"] = route_hint
```

sam: I like the opt-in header idea. Console/telemetry should also expose an attribution tag so we can query "requests where both headers were present" and verify the shim before broader rollout.

kai: For TS/Go we'll mirror the same opt-in API (sdkConfig.compatRouteShim = true). Important: make the default OFF for minor releases and ON for patch releases only. We can't risk breaking existing enterprise customers.

jonas: Implementation plan from infra side: (1) add `X-Rwd-Attr-Prefer` handling in gateway (no-op unless header present), (2) add server-side flag to enforce deterministic precedence `/api/v1/flags/routing_precedence`, (3) ship SDK shims behind a feature flag. Canary the gateway change in `canary-03` region.

maria: Timeline proposal: ship SDK patch (opt-in) this week, enable gateway header handling in canary for 24h, then enable server flag in canary and monitor `quota_misattribution_rate` and `console.attribution_discrepancy` (new telemetry). If metrics are stable for 48h, roll to staging and then prod.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: gateway/canary-03 -> 2026-03-21T16:00Z. Rolling canary will create a trace sampling tag `rwd.route_compat_canary=true`.

sam: Also add a console small UX change — when two attribution headers are present, show both and highlight which one was used. That will reduce support churn while we roll shims.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a tiny console PR for the dual-header panel and add samples for the query. Thanks all. :seedling:
